featured_reviews.name: Deepika Pai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sardar Pavbhaji, the oldest pav bhaji hotel in Tadeo, is a must-visit for all pav bhaji lovers. Known for their delicious pav bhaji, they serve up a perfect blend of quality and generous portions.
The inviting environment and cooperative staff enhance your dining experience, making it a popular spot for locals and visitors alike.
With an authentic taste that highlights the perfect balance of spices in their bhaji, each bite is a delight.
Whether you're craving a quick snack or a hearty meal, Sardar Pavbhaji promises satisfaction every time.
Don't miss out on savoring their signature dish that continues to delight patrons year after year!

Went to Café Noorani a few days ago and had a lovely experience. The lamb biryani was absolutely delicious—full of flavour and very satisfying.

Instead of helping or suggesting alternatives, he repeatedly responded in a rude tone saying “hamare yaha nahi milta hai” and “pata hi nahi hai.” What was surprising is that despite being in the hospitality industry, he didn’t even seem aware of similar starter items available in their own restaurant.

The interaction was so unpleasant that I decided to leave immediately and even complained to the manager. Unfortunately, the manager seemed completely uninterested and did not handle the situation professionally either.

If you stay in SoBo (South Bombay), you'd swear by Manju's Samosa Sandwich! Well, if you think of it, it's just samosa smashed inside two slices of bread with some sliced salad, but if you happen to meet Manju, and if you happen to know the years he's steadily served what would probably be lakhs of sandwiches, you'd know there's emotions and nostalgia attached to it, needless to say the sandwiches are delicious too!
Dishing out sandwiches for over three decades, has earned Manju a permanent mark on Google maps if not for anything else. He still has his rudimentary, make shift set up, and serves nominally priced sandwiches with a big smile on his face!
Try taking a picture of his sandwich and see him gloriously smile and give his history out with pride!
Surely this man knows how to personify satisfaction in doing what you love. It's definitely selling sandwiches for him!

We noticed many varieties of cream puddings displayed, which looked very tempting. Since it was our first time, we asked the staff which one was the best, and they suggested the Seetha Phal (custard apple) cream pudding, so we ordered that along with rose milk falooda.
As they said, the Seetha Phal cream pudding was extraordinary and super in taste, very rich and satisfying. The rose milk falooda was good, but not as special as the pudding. They also serve many other juices, desserts, and snacks.
Prices are definitely on the higher side, and most items feel expensive. The ambience is simple and nothing fancy, and the service is just okay. Overall, the Seetha Phal cream pudding is highly recommended if you visit here.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
A perennial favorite among locals and tourists alike, Haji Ali Juice Centre is an iconic culinary landmark nestled at the threshold of the historic Haji Ali Dargah. Since its inception in the 1960s, this bustling establishment has cultivated a legendary status, evolving from a modest stop for pilgrims into a vibrant gastronomic institution. It is celebrated for its unwavering commitment to quality, utilizing fresh, seasonal ingredients to craft an extensive repertoire of refreshments that have become synonymous with Mumbai's street food culture.
Reviewers frequently highlight the establishment's ability to maintain high standards of hygiene and flavor despite the immense daily crowds. The atmosphere is quintessentially Mumbai—a high-energy, casual setting where patrons often enjoy their treats standing on the pavement or from the comfort of their cars, adding a unique drive-in charm to the experience.
• Signature Fruit Creams: The "Sitaphal" (custard apple) cream is universally acclaimed as a must-try masterpiece, featuring a luscious, thick consistency generously laden with fresh fruit chunks.
• Exotic Shakes & Juices: Guests often praise the Mango Milkshake for its rich, creamy texture and the "Triveni"—a sophisticated blend of mango, strawberry, and kiwi juices.
• Savoury Accompaniments: Beyond beverages, the menu boasts popular fusion snacks like the Jain Pizza and the indulgent Cheese Toast, noted for its generous cheese-to-bread ratio.
• Late-Night Accessibility: Operating from the early morning until well past midnight, it serves as a reliable sanctuary for night revelers seeking high-quality refreshments.

featured_reviews.name: Sanoop ks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Haji Ali Juice Centre is one of those places in Mumbai that almost everyone has heard about, and naturally, expectations are quite high before visiting. The menu is extensive, filled with a wide variety of juices, shakes, and desserts that look appealing at first glance. The taste of the items is definitely good—fresh, flavorful, and satisfying to an extent. You can tell that the ingredients are of decent quality and prepared well.

However, beyond that initial impression, nothing truly stands out. There isn’t anything particularly unique or memorable about the flavors that would make you want to come back again and again. It feels like what you get is something you could easily find at many other juice shops across the city.

One of the biggest drawbacks is how overhyped the place feels. Because of its popularity and constant crowd, you go in expecting something exceptional, but the experience turns out to be fairly average. This mismatch between expectation and reality is quite noticeable.

On top of that, the pricing feels a bit on the higher side for what is offered. While the quality is decent, it doesn’t quite justify the cost, making it seem overrated.

Overall, Haji Ali Juice Centre delivers good taste but nothing extraordinary. It’s worth trying once for the experience, but it may not live up to the hype surrounding it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is a great pick in breach candy if you’re craving Pure Veg Mexican flavors with a creative twist. Started with the Cantina Nachos made with gluten-free corn—they were perfectly crunchy, fresh, and loaded with cheese. The Tex Mex Classic Burger was a highlight, with a crispy potato patty paired beautifully with black beans, cheese sauce, fresh salsa, guacamole, and pickled onions—every bite had a nice balance of textures and flavors.

The Guacamole Toast was simple yet delicious, a healthier option that didn’t compromise on taste. But the real surprise was the Mexican Pizza—super unique with a cheesy base at the bottom and top, layered with salsa in between. It’s something you don’t come across often and definitely worth trying.

For drinks, the Mango Inferno stood out with its sweet and spicy combination, especially with that bold hit of red chillies. The Jalamelon was equally refreshing—juicy watermelon with a hint of jalapeños giving it a nice kick.

Ended the meal with the Quattro Leche dessert, a rich and indulgent take on the classic three-milk dessert, and it was the perfect way to wrap things up.

On top of the food, the place offers comfortable indoor as well as outdoor seating, making it ideal for both casual hangouts and relaxed dining. Overall, a well-rounded experience with good food, interesting flavors, and a chill vibe.

The Vibe
The outdoor seating is a total mood, featuring lush greenery and twinkling fairy lights that make it perfect for a relaxed evening. Inside, the decor flips to a vibrant, colorful "Mexico" theme with fun wall art that’s practically made for Instagram.
The Food
• Nachos: These are a must-try. They come loaded with a generous amount of creamy cheese, fresh salsa, and veggies. Every chip has a perfect crunch.
• Burritos & Burgers: The portions are hearty. The burrito is packed with flavor and tightly wrapped, while the burger features a thick, well-seasoned patty with fresh greens.
• Cheese Fries: Crinkle-cut and absolutely drenched in a rich cheese sauce—pure comfort food.
• Chocolate Massacre: To end on a high note, this dessert is a chocolate lover's dream. It’s rich, gooey, and lives up to its name in the best way possible.
The Drinks
Their bottled beverages, like the Fizzarito and Lymang Magic, are incredibly refreshing and serve as the perfect palate cleanser between spicy bites.
Final Verdict
Whether you’re looking for a quick takeaway or a cute spot for a casual date night, this place is a solid choice. Great portions, vibrant atmosphere, and authentic flavors.

Recommended: Loaded Nachos and the Chocolate Massacre! 🌯🍫✨

featured_reviews.name: Salah Busalem
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great breakfast experience at Plate & Pint in Mumbai. The welcome was warm, the service was professional, and all the orders arrived correctly, on time, and with very good quality.

The breakfast was delicious overall, and I really liked that the restaurant offers both morning and afternoon menus, giving plenty of variety to choose from. It was also nice to see that they have gluten-free items available, which makes the menu more inclusive and thoughtful for different dietary preferences.

I also ordered dessert, and it was a great experience — especially the molten chocolate, which was excellent.

The only dish I personally didn’t enjoy much was the shakshoka, as it was a bit too runny for my preference. Also, the restaurant is pet-friendly, which may be a positive for many guests, although it is personally not my preferred atmosphere.

Other than that, everything was enjoyable and well prepared. I’ll also be sharing the food photos and recipes because the presentation and flavors were worth remembering. Definitely a place I’d visit again for breakfast and desserts.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An unforgettable Thai brunch experience that truly transported us straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok 🇹🇭✨
We recently attended the Tuk Tuk Tales pop-up at Plate & Pint curated by the incredibly talented Chef Akanksha Saigal, and every single dish on the menu reflected her passion, creativity, and deep understanding of authentic Thai flavours.
We went as a group of friends for brunch, and honestly, it turned into one of those meals where every plate sparks conversation, every bite feels memorable, and time just flies by over great food and even better company. The vibe at Plate & Pint added so much warmth to the experience — lively, cozy, vibrant, and perfect for a long indulgent afternoon.
The meal began with the Mango & Avocado Ceviche — incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced with chilli, lime, cilantro, green apple, and crispy shallots adding layers of texture and zing. A refreshing start that instantly awakened the palate.
The Crispy Potato Stacks were an absolute standout. Perfectly crisp with rich green curry notes, aromatic fried basil, chilli crackling, and toasted herb rice bringing together comfort and complexity in every bite.
The Gai Yang Thai BBQ Chicken was beautifully charred and deeply flavourful, paired wonderfully with pickled cucumber, pickled chilli, and a delicious dipping sauce that elevated the smokiness of the chicken.
The Spicy Tamarind Glaze dishes were another highlight. Both the cottage cheese and pork belly versions were packed with bold sweet spicy flavours and had that addictive Thai style balance that keeps you reaching for another bite.
For mains, the Holy Basil Stir Fry was pure comfort food done right. Fragrant basil, juicy chicken, cucumber, fluffy rice, and a fried egg made this dish hearty, satisfying, and incredibly soulful.
The Tom Yum Hot Pot was bursting with authentic Thai aromatics — lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf — with the prawns soaking beautifully in the deeply comforting broth. Warm, sharp, spicy, and layered with flavour.
And of course, no Thai meal feels complete without a great Pad Thai, and this one absolutely delivered. Perfectly cooked rice noodles coated in tamarind sauce with chicken, bean sprouts, and peanuts creating the ideal balance of sweet, savoury, nutty, and tangy flavours.
Dessert was the perfect finale — Mango Sticky Rice with tender coconut ice cream. Rich, fragrant, comforting, and tropical all at once. Easily one of the best versions we’ve had in Mumbai.
The cocktails were equally thoughtful and fun, especially the Thai Chilli Guava Michelada and Mango Chilli White Wine Spritz, which paired beautifully with the food and added another vibrant layer to the entire experience.
Huge compliments to Chef Akanksha for creating such a well executed pop-up that didn’t just serve food, but genuinely told a story through flavours. Every dish felt curated with heart and authenticity.
Thank you for inviting us and giving us such a memorable afternoon filled with laughter, amazing conversations, delicious food, and beautiful hospitality. Experiences like these are exactly why food brings people together so effortlessly.

Already looking forward to the next one ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Suryaprakash Barnwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College, Dadar definitely attracts a huge crowd. We reached around 2:15 PM and still had to wait close to 40 minutes in the queue before getting served, which itself shows how popular the place is.

The location is definitely a plus point since it’s close to Dadar Beach. The highlight for me was the crispy chura, which added a unique crunch and gave the vada pav a different texture compared to regular stalls.

However, the overall experience felt a bit overrated for the wait and pricing. The service was slow, there was no extra chutney or extra chura provided, and the vada pavs were simply wrapped in paper and handed over. Since everything is pre-made, there’s almost no scope for customization in terms of chutney or spice level like you usually get at local vendors. Personally, I also found the taste slightly too sweet.

The pricing is ₹35 for a single vada pav and ₹140 for four pieces, which feels almost double compared to many other local vendors offering similar or even better taste.

Overall, it’s worth trying once for the hype and experience, but personally I don’t think the taste and service justify waiting more than 40 minutes when there are plenty of local places serving equally good vada pav with faster service, better customization, and more value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Shreyash Bidave
featured_reviews.review_text:
After taking blessings at Shree Siddhivinayak Temple, a visit to Ashok Vada Pav is almost a ritual for food lovers. The vada pav here is served hot and fresh, with a perfectly crispy vada, soft pav, and flavorful chutneys that make every bite memorable.
One of the best experiences is to take a parcel and head towards Dadar Chowpatty. Sitting by the sea, enjoying the view and cool breeze while eating this iconic vada pav creates a combination that's hard to beat. The joy of having Ashok Vada Pav with the sea view is something truly special.
The long queue outside the stall speaks for itself. Just looking at the crowd, you can tell how popular this place is. It's not famous without reason—the taste, consistency, and quality have made it a favorite among Mumbaikars and tourists alike for years.
If you're in Mumbai, this is a must-try street food experience. For many people, Ashok Vada Pav isn't just a snack; it's a part of Mumbai's food culture and one of the most famous vada pav destinations in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Puneet Arora
featured_reviews.review_text: A must-visit spot for vada pav lovers, located within walking distance from Siddhivinayak Temple. The queue is usually quite long, so some patience is required, but the taste makes it totally worth the wait. The vada pav is fresh, flavourful, and consistently good, offering great value at just ₹30 per piece. Despite the crowd, the service is fairly quick and well-managed. featured_reviews.name: Arun
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally tried the famous Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College. Here is my honest take:

The Good part:
• Location: It is located very close to Dadar Beach. It’s nice to grab your order and go for a short walk by the sea.
• Texture: The combination of the vada with the crispy "chura" is definitely interesting and adds a nice crunch.

The Not-So-Good:
• The Wait: Be prepared to stand in line. It took me between 20-30 minutes just to get served.
• Taste & Customization: Because the Vada Pavs are pre-made, there is hardly any room for customization. Unlike other local shops where you can adjust the chutney to your liking, here you get what you get. Personally, I found the taste a bit too salty and sweet for my palate.

The Price:
• ₹30 per piece
• ₹60 for a plate (2 Vada Pavs)

Verdict: While it’s not "bad," I don't think it is worth a 30-minute wait, especially when other local spots offer better customization.

featured_reviews.review_text: Hands down one of the tastiest vada pav you’ll find in Mumbai. The vada is perfectly crispy outside, soft inside, and packed with flavour. featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a city that runs on speed, spice, and soul, some places don’t just serve food, they become emotion. Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College is exactly that kind of institution, where generations have stood shoulder to shoulder, waiting for that one perfect bite.
What makes their vada pav truly iconic is the balance. The batata vada is crisp on the outside, soft and flavourful inside, with just the right hint of garlic and spice. The pav is always fresh, lightly toasted, and acts as the perfect carrier without overpowering the star.
But the real magic lies in their chutney game. That signature dry garlic chutney hits instantly with a bold, smoky spice, while the fried green chillies on the side elevate the entire experience. It’s not just heat, it’s character, the kind that lingers and keeps you coming back.
And then comes the cult favourite, the chura pav. Buttery, spicy, slightly messy, and absolutely addictive. The crushed vada mixed with chutneys and masala, soaked into the pav, creates a texture and flavour bomb that feels indulgent in the most Mumbai way possible. Crisp edges, soft centres, and that unmistakable street-style richness.
Being a true Dadarkar, I’ve grown up eating this vada pav, and what’s incredible is how the taste has remained exactly the same over the years, still the best vada pav, hands down.
There’s a legacy here that you can actually taste. Started decades ago and now run by the next generation, Ashok Vada Pav has become a landmark in Dadar’s food scene. It has seen college crowds, office rush, late-night hunger, and everything in between, yet the consistency remains untouched. No unnecessary reinvention, just doing the basics exceptionally well, every single time. The vibe is classic Mumbai, fast-moving queues, minimal waiting despite the crowd, and an energy that feels alive. You don’t come here for luxury, you come here for authenticity.
Ashok Vada Pav isn’t just food, it’s a ritual, a memory, and for many, a weekly craving that never fades.
Simple, iconic, and absolutely unbeatable. 🌶️🔥
